newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada posts healthy budget surplus in June.
newsitem.headline: Canada posts healthy budget surplus in June.

text.p: Canada on Friday reported its second straight monthly budget surplus, signalling that the country is well ahead of schedule in its fight to balance its books, economists said.
The Finance Department said the country recorded a surplus of C$1.50 billion ($1.08 billion) in June, compared with a C$653 million ($469 million) deficit a year earlier.
In May, the budget surplus was C$1.37 billion ($986 million), compared with a year earlier deficit of C$582 million ($419 million).
It was the first time since the late 1970s that budget surpluses were posted for two straight months, the Finance Department said.

"There was no question that the budget numbers were improving rapidly, but this puts things into perspective how fast the improvement is," Doug Porter, senior economist at brokerage Nesbitt Burns, told Reuters.
"We thought we had been somewhat on the optimistic side calling for a full-year deficit of this (fiscal) year of C$5 billion ($3.6 billion), and it looks like Ottawa may do better than that."
The government's year-to-date deficit for fiscal 1998 ending March 31 plunged to C$533 million ($384 million) from year ago C$5.30 billion ($3.6 bln).
Canada's Finance Minister Paul Martin has projected a budget deficit of C$17 billion ($12.2 billion) for this fiscal year.
Martin has said the deficit for the fiscal year that ended March 31, 1997 would be under C$16 billion ($11.5 billion), but the final numbers will not be available until this autumn.
The government said the latest monthly surplus was linked to lower spending, coupled with rising revenues from taxes.
"It's the best of both worlds right now," said Bank of Nova Scotia economist Aron Gampel, citing recent strong economic growth along with sharp cutbacks in government spending.
"These numbers illustrate that the government is winning on all sides of the deficit battle."
He said the surplus would likely prompt calls from Canadians for the government to loosen its purse strings after years of spending cuts.
Martin has slashed the budget deficit steadily since his Liberal government took office in 1993. The deficit then was about C$43 billion ($31 billion).
The Liberals, who were re-elected last June, have said they would eliminate the deficit within two years. Martin has said he would update the government's deficit projections this autumn.
